nodes.title: Cover and contents
nodes.summary: The cover page of InterGlobe Aviation’s FY24 annual report announces the 21st Annual General Meeting, provides the AGM date and venue, and confirms that the report and AGM notice are available electronically and on the company website. It contains key corporate facts and figures such as the company’s symbol and scrip code, the AGM schedule, regulatory compliance details, and contact information for the company secretary and chief compliance officer, while also indicating that the full report will include financial metrics (revenue, operating income), fleet size, risk disclosures, and board composition.

nodes.title: Giving wings
nodes.summary: The “Giving wings” section of InterGlobe Aviation’s FY24 annual report highlights a record‑breaking year for IndiGo, showcasing key financial metrics such as a ₹689,043 million profit after tax, ₹81,725 million revenue from operations, and a 26.6 % EBITDAR of ₹175,447 million, alongside non‑financial achievements like 107 million customers, 2,016 daily flights, and a 85.9 % load factor. It also provides operational facts—fleet size of 367 aircraft, 121 destinations, 3.7 million+ departures, and 37,200 employees (44 % women)—and governance details, including board composition, risk disclosures, and sustainability initiatives.

nodes.title: Giving wings  to the nation
nodes.summary: InterGlobe Aviation’s FY24 “Giving wings to the nation” section highlights IndiGo’s rapid expansion—now operating 367 aircraft and ordering 985 more to reach a 600‑plus fleet by 2030—while underscoring its role as India’s preferred low‑cost carrier with an 81.3 % on‑time performance in DGCA metros. The narrative blends strategic ambitions (global aviation leadership, domestic and international network growth, AI‑driven customer service) with key metrics such as fleet size, order backlog, on‑time performance, and the company’s purpose, vision, and mission statements.

nodes.title: Leading the way  towards new  heights and across  new frontiers
nodes.summary: InterGlobe Aviation’s FY 2024 Annual Report highlights a year of record growth under its “Towards new heights and across new frontiers” strategy, noting milestones such as welcoming 100 million customers, flying to 115 destinations, operating 2,000 daily flights, and serving over 300,000 passengers each day. The section presents a mix of quantitative data—revenue, fleet expansion (500‑aircraft order, 30 A350‑900s, projected 600+ aircraft by 2030), passenger and flight metrics, and risk disclosures—alongside qualitative insights on strategic pillars (Reassure, Develop, Create), board leadership, and global market positioning.

nodes.title: Where we operate Connecting the world,  one dot at a time
nodes.summary: InterGlobe Aviation’s FY24 annual report outlines its global footprint, noting that as of June 2024 the airline serves 88 domestic destinations and 30 + international destinations across Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, Africa, and the Far East, with a total of 13,475 weekly flights. The section also highlights key operational metrics such as 456 weekly flights to 12 Middle‑East destinations, 169 weekly flights to 12 South‑East Asian destinations, and 88 weekly flights to 12 Central‑Asian destinations, while noting the presence of 8 codeshare partners and the inclusion of 3 inactive destinations pre‑COVID.
headings: Where we operate Connecting the world,  one dot at a time
Where we operate Connecting the world,  one dot at a time

nodes.title: Key milestones Our incredible journey  so far
nodes.summary: The “Key milestones – Our incredible journey so far” section chronicles IndiGo’s rapid growth from its 2006 IPO to its 2024 peak, highlighting pivotal moments such as the delivery of its 100th and 200th aircraft, the launch of international routes, the first profitable year, and the expansion to over 300 aircraft and 100+ destinations. It contains a mix of quantitative facts—fleet size, number of daily flights, customer count, revenue milestones, and order volumes—as well as qualitative milestones like codeshare agreements, freighter operations, and strategic market entries.

nodes.title: Efficiency  at the helm
nodes.summary: The “Efficiency at the helm” section highlights InterGlobe Aviation’s (IndiGo) modern, fuel‑efficient fleet of 367 aircraft, of which 78 % are Airbus A320neo models that deliver a 15 % fuel‑efficiency gain, and notes a robust order book of 985 aircraft to support future growth. It provides key facts and figures such as fleet size, average age (4.4 years), aircraft mix (A320neo, A321neo, A320ceo, ATR, A321 freighter, B777), passenger and tonnage capacities, and underscores the company’s commitment to sustainability and operational excellence.

nodes.title: Key performance indicators Financial highlights
nodes.summary: The FY24 Key Performance Indicators section presents a concise snapshot of IndiGo’s financial and operational health, showing year‑on‑year revenue, EBITDAR margin, profit after tax, total cash, available seat kilometres, load factor, employee count, and fleet size. It contains quantitative figures such as millions of rupees for revenue and cash, percentage margins, and absolute counts for seats, employees, and aircraft, while also highlighting trends and risks that underpin the airline’s growth strategy.

nodes.title: Ensuring a hassle-free  experience
nodes.summary: The “Ensuring a hassle‑free experience” section highlights IndiGo’s customer‑centric initiatives—from AI‑driven booking channels and multilingual support to revamped in‑flight catering and community‑building campaigns—while underscoring its commitment to safety, inclusivity, and service excellence. It contains quantitative and qualitative facts such as NPS scores, on‑time performance rankings, fleet‑size references, revenue‑impacting fare strategies, and risk‑management insights, all framed within the broader context of stakeholder value creation and board‑level oversight.

nodes.title: Powering growth together
nodes.summary: The “Powering growth together” section highlights IndiGo’s commitment to a diverse, inclusive workforce and its new Gurugram headquarters, underscoring how a culture built on five core values and the “6E Embrace” DEI strategy drives service excellence and employee satisfaction. It presents quantitative facts such as the growth of employees with disabilities (from 11 in FY 2022 to 200 in FY 2024), the current 18 % female leadership and 44 % overall female representation, and the target of 25 % female leadership by 2025, while also outlining strategic initiatives, risk‑mitigation through inclusive hiring, and the impact on corporate reputation.
headings: IndiGo unveils new corporate  headquarters in Gurugram
IndiGo unveils new corporate  headquarters in Gurugram

nodes.title: Reaching out to the  community
nodes.summary: IndiGoReach, the airline’s CSR arm, reports that its women‑empowerment and environmental programmes have reached 41,000 women, 1,000 transgenders, 24,300 households, and 5,200 self‑help groups, with participants’ incomes rising 20‑25 % and fuel‑wood consumption dropping 55 % through biogas and smokeless cookstove adoption. The section provides quantitative impact metrics (e.g., number of beneficiaries, income uplift, household reach, and emission‑reduction percentages) alongside qualitative descriptions of community transformation and the airline’s commitment to social responsibility.

nodes.title: 13,500  children benefitted
nodes.summary: The FY24 report highlights IndiGo’s CSR impact, noting that 13,500 children benefited from education programmes that included digital literacy, science labs, libraries, and WASH facilities, while employees also volunteered in blood drives, senior‑citizen visits, tree‑planting, and mentorship initiatives under the Vision 2030 “IndiGoReach 3 E” framework. The section contains quantitative facts such as the number of children served, the 1 million‑tree plantation goal, and the 40 locations involved, alongside qualitative details on board‑led strategic goals, risk‑mitigation through environmental stewardship, and financial commitments to sustainability and community development.

nodes.title: 19% Reduced emissions  vs FY 2016 FY 20 FY 16 FY 21 FY 17 FY 22 FY 18 FY 23 FY 19 FY 24
nodes.summary: IndiGo’s FY24 annual report highlights a 19 % reduction in emissions versus FY2016, driven by electrification of ground vehicles, adoption of renewable energy at learning centres, and innovative water‑saving nozzles that cut on‑board consumption by up to 98 %; the report also reports a 66 % efficiency gain in EV use, 50,000 metric‑tonne CO₂ avoided, and the first airport (Ahmedabad) achieving a 100 % fleet of eco‑friendly electric coaches. The section contains quantitative data on emissions trends, fleet electrification, waste‑management metrics, and governance details such as the ESG Task Force, board oversight, and compliance with SEBI BRSR and DGCA CORSIA reporting, underscoring IndiGo’s commitment to environmental performance, operational efficiency, and transparent ESG disclosure.

nodes.title: Board of Directors
nodes.summary: The Board of Directors section lists the 11 directors of InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo), including four independent directors, three non‑executive directors, and the Managing Director, and it outlines the governance structure and the composition of the Management Executive Committee. It contains factual details such as the names and titles of each director, the board’s composition (independent, non‑executive, and executive members), and the roles of key executive officers, but it does not provide quantitative figures like revenue, fleet size, or risk metrics.

nodes.title: Turning miles into  milestones
nodes.summary: InterGlobe Aviation’s FY24 report highlights a series of industry accolades, noting that IndiGo was named Airline of the Year at the Air Transport Awards 2024, received the CAPA Environmental Sustainability Award, and earned the Best Low‑Cost Airline title for the 14th consecutive year, while also being recognized for its DEI Champion Award and its status as the world’s youngest aircraft fleet in the 100+ aircraft category. The section contains qualitative facts—such as award titles and recognitions—and quantitative indicators like the number of consecutive awards, fleet size category, and brand ranking, all underscoring the airline’s market positioning and stakeholder value creation.

It contains quantitative facts and figures such as projected GDP growth rates (e.g., 3.2 % global, 7.8 % India), inflation data, monetary policy decisions, and references to the company’s fleet size, financial performance, risk factors, and board composition.

nodes.title: Board's Report
nodes.summary: The Board’s Report (pages 59‑76) presents IndiGo’s FY 2024 financial performance, noting a 27.47 % rise in total income to ₹712,311.63 million and a turnaround from a net loss to a net profit of ₹81,724.68 million, alongside detailed earnings per share figures and a comprehensive income statement. It also outlines subsidiary results—Agile Airport Services’ revenue growth and profit decline, and the newly incorporated IAFS’s pending operations—while highlighting key risks, governance details, and board composition.
headings: Report of the Board of Directors
Report of the Board of Directors

nodes.title: Corporate Governance Report
nodes.summary: The Corporate Governance Report (pp. 77‑98) outlines InterGlobe Aviation’s commitment to integrity, transparency, accountability and ethics, detailing the Board’s composition (8 directors: 4 independent, 3 non‑executive, 1 executive) and the governance framework that includes codes of conduct, compliance with SEBI LODR regulations, and procedures for board induction and decision‑making. It contains factual data on board structure, percentages of director categories, and governance policies, while also highlighting risks, regulatory obligations, and the company’s strategic oversight mechanisms.

headings: Declaration on Compliance of Code of Conduct

nodes.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (pages 99-122)
nodes.summary: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (FY 2024) outlines IndiGo’s long‑term value‑building strategy, detailing its commitment to responsible business practices, ESG governance, and the implementation of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct. It contains quantitative facts and figures on revenue, fleet size (367 aircraft), passenger traffic (~106.7 million), carbon emissions, safety metrics, and risk management, as well as qualitative disclosures on board composition, leadership indicators, and third‑party assurance of core sustainability data.

nodes.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (pages 123-140)
nodes.summary: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (pages 123‑140) outlines IndiGo’s approach to health and safety, stakeholder engagement, and value‑chain assessment, reporting that only one employee suffered a high‑consequence injury in FY 2024 and was rehabilitated, with no workers affected, and that the company does not offer transition assistance for retirements or terminations. It contains quantitative facts such as employee injury counts, the percentage of value‑chain partners assessed (nil), and qualitative details on stakeholder identification, engagement frequency, and communication channels, while also noting the absence of corrective actions for partner health‑and‑safety risks.

nodes.title: Independent Auditor's Report
nodes.summary: The Independent Auditor’s Report confirms that InterGlobe Aviation Limited’s standalone financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2024 present a true and fair view in accordance with Indian GAAP and the Companies Act, 2013, and that the audit was conducted in compliance with the Standards on Auditing and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India’s Code of Ethics. It contains factual details such as the company’s balance sheet, profit and loss, cash‑flow and equity statements, key audit matters (e.g., passenger revenue recognition, lease accounting, and related‑party transactions), and the auditor’s assessment of material misstatement risks, all of which underpin the audit opinion.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The Standalone Financial Statements (pages 155‑160) present IndiGo’s balance sheet as of 31 March 2024, showing total assets of ₹590.4 billion, equity of ₹451.3 billion, and liabilities of ₹139.1 billion, with a detailed breakdown of non‑current assets (property, plant, equipment, right‑of‑use assets, investments, and deferred tax assets) and current assets (inventories, trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents). The section also lists key financial metrics such as the company’s cash‑equivalent position, lease liabilities, borrowings, and provisions, while highlighting governance elements like the composition of the board, risk disclosures (e.g., liquidity, credit, and regulatory risks), and the impact of capital structure on financial stability.

The section includes key figures such as total non‑current assets (₹463.7 bn), current assets (₹358.5 bn), and highlights risks and governance through notes on deferred tax, income tax assets, and other non‑current items, while also providing a snapshot of the board’s oversight and the company’s financial position.

The section also outlines the fair‑value hierarchy (Level 1, 2, 3), highlights the carrying values and amortised costs of various financial instruments, and references related disclosures such as risk factors, board composition, and fleet size, giving a comprehensive snapshot of the company’s financial position and governance for the year ended 31 March 2024.

nodes.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (pages 299-301)
nodes.summary: The “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” (pages 299‑301) provide a concise snapshot of InterGlobe Aviation’s newly incorporated subsidiary, InterGlobe Aviation Financial Services IFSC Private Limited, including its acquisition date (12 Oct 2023), reporting period (12 Oct 2023‑31 Mar 2024), authorised and paid‑up capital, and the fact that it has no assets, liabilities, turnover or profit yet. It also lists the composition of the Board of Directors, key executive appointments, and the statutory and internal audit firms, giving a clear view of governance, capital structure, and the absence of associate companies or joint ventures.

nodes.title: Notice of Annual General Meeting
nodes.summary: The Notice of Annual General Meeting (pages 302‑315) announces that InterGlobe Aviation’s 21st AGM will be held on 23 August 2024 via video conferencing to approve the audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY 2024, appoint and re‑appoint directors and auditors, and re‑appoint an independent director. It contains key facts and figures such as the company’s financial results for the year ended 31 March 2024, the composition and rotation of the board, the appointment of the statutory auditors for a five‑year term, and the re‑appointment of an independent director, all framed within the statutory and listing regulatory context.
